key_insight: Chaos-induced dephasing enables polynomial-time classical estimation of four- and eight-point OTOCs in typical 1D random quantum circuits.
engineering_relevance: The algorithm provides a classical benchmark for OTOC-based quantum advantage claims in 1D chaotic circuits.
method: Expand each OTOC into a rapidly converging series in replicated Hilbert space.
Compute leading contributions from histories within permutation degrees of freedom.
Exploit chaos-induced dephasing to suppress corrections from excursions outside that space.
evidence_signal: Theoretical and numerical evidence supports correction suppression, while implementations achieve high accuracy in 1D and higher signal-to-noise at larger depths than recent Google 2D experiments.
watch_item: Extension to higher dimensions remains open, so the results do not resolve quantum advantage for 2D OTOCs.
paper_title: An efficient classical algorithm for OTOCs in chaotic quantum dynamics
